excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: You could use https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/blob-archiver - it can read blobs from any CL and store them them in a simple directory or on S3 and then exposes the same getter APIs as a CL would so it's easy to pull the data back out when needed.

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: this doesn't work if we don't have any working CL though, right

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: True, but you could configure CLs to prune blobs and this would cover the archive requirements for you.

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: I think there's still a bootstrap problem, can't seed the blob-archiver if there's no working node

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: our LH nodes that were blob archives are completely dead

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: maybe with an offline migration they could export their data to blob-archiver though

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: could be worth a try

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: hmm, yeah that would mean it couldn't fetch the full history.  It should be ok to start from now and archive going forward though. Of course, something has to be pushing the network forward - I'm assuming nodes would work if they weren't trying to archive blobs.

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: yes, it's the 4TB DB that is fatal for us

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: the use-case we have is that QuickNode want all archived blobs on all networks, not just from now on

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: I thought we'd been running our archiver since before blobs started on sepolia and mainnet at least. To be honest, I haven't actually looked at the status of it for quite a while though - in practice we really only need about 30 days of history in an absolute worst case.
